title: Architecture & Standards — Canonical Guidelines and ADRs
author: Avery Martinez
body:
Overview
========
This document defines Redwood Inference's canonical architecture and engineering standards across API design, coding, infrastructure (IaC), model-serving, observability, and performance. It consolidates stable guidance teams should follow and provides an ADR (architecture decision record) template plus a set of recent decisions. The goal is to ensure consistent, secure, and measurable delivery of inference services with predictable economics and operational characteristics.

Scope
-----
Applies to all services, runtime components, libraries, and infra changes that affect: hosted API endpoints, Dedicated runtime services, Private deployment artifacts, shared infra modules, and public SDKs. Exceptions require an ADR and explicit approval from the Architecture Working Group.

Principles
----------
- Developer-first: make correct behavior easy and consistent across repos.
- Observable by default: every change ships with metrics, traces, and log structure.
- Secure by design: follow least privilege, vault-backed secrets, and CI policy gates.
- Backward-compatible: prioritize non-breaking changes and provide deprecation windows.
- Cost-aware: prefer designs that make unit economics visible and tunable.

1) API Standards
----------------
Purpose: Ensure reliable, discoverable, and versioned API surfaces for external and internal consumers.
Key rules:
- Surface types: REST + JSON for public APIs, gRPC for high-throughput internal services.
- Naming: resources are plural, kebab-case for HTTP paths, e.g. /v1/models/{model-id}/infer.
- Versioning: major version in path (/v1/). Backwards-incompatible changes require a new major.
- Schemas: publish OpenAPI v3 for all public REST endpoints and keep generator tests in CI.
- Error model: 4xx for client errors with structured JSON {"code":"<KEY>", "message":"...", "details":{}}. 5xx reserved for platform/service failures.
- Idempotency: POSTs that create long-running workloads must accept an Idempotency-Key header.
- Rate-limiting headers: include X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset for all public endpoints.
- Streaming: server-sent events or chunked HTTP for streaming token deltas; include content-type application/stream+json and explicit event framing.
- Security: all public APIs require mTLS or bearer tokens; use short-lived tokens issued by the control plane.
- Client SDKs: generated from OpenAPI and should be published to the mono-repo SDK registry; breaking changes require synced SDK release notes.

Example endpoint specification snippet (OpenAPI-style):

POST /v1/models/{model_id}/infer
- path params: model_id (string)
- body: {"input": "string", "max_tokens": 256, "temperature": 0.0} 
- responses: 200 -> {"request_id":"<id>", "outputs":[{"text":"..."}], "model_version":"..."} 

2) Coding Standards
-------------------
Languages in primary services: Go (platform control-plane), Rust/C++ (runtime kernels), Python/TypeScript for SDKs and glue.
Mandatory checks:
- Formatting: gofmt/gofumpt, rustfmt, black/ruff for Python, prettier/eslint for TS.
- Linting: CI enforces linters and denies merges on new high-severity findings.
- Testing: unit tests + integration tests; target >= 80% coverage for core services, 65% for SDKs.
- Type safety: prefer static types where practical (Go/TS/ Rust). Python services should include strict mypy checks on public modules.
- PR guidance: max 400 lines changed when possible; PR description must include motivation, rollout plan, and rollback steps.
- Commit messages: follow Conventional Commits (feat|fix|chore|refactor|docs|test|perf): scope - short desc.
- Dependency management: prefer pinned versions and Dependabot for minor/patch updates; major upgrades require ADR and a compatibility test matrix run.

3) Infrastructure (IaC) Standards
--------------------------------
- Terraform is canonical for cloud infra. Modules must live in /eng-infra/terraform-modules and be reusable across accounts.
- Naming & Tags: resources include tags {owner, team, env, cost-center, project}. Standard tag keys: Owner, Team, Environment, CostCenter, Project.
- Secrets & Keys: never store secrets in VCS. Use Vault (transit for encryption) and KMS for keys.
- Account boundaries: production workloads run in isolated cloud accounts; non-prod may share dev accounts with quotas.
- Network: default to least-privilege VPC rules; use private subnets for inference nodes and VPC endpoints for control-plane connections.
- Drift & Drift Detection: enable tfplan scans in CI and periodic drift detection jobs in each environment (daily).
- Blue/green supported: infra modules should enable safe rollouts (i.e., target group switching, immutable infra where feasible).

IaC example conventions table:
| Resource | Name pattern | Required tags | TTL / Notes |
|---------|--------------|---------------|-------------|
| EC2/ECS task | redwood-{team}-{service}-{env}-{shortid} | Owner, Team, Environment, CostCenter | N/A |
| S3 bucket | rwd-{env}-{project}-{purpose} | Owner, Team, Environment | versioning enabled |

4) Model-serving Standards
-------------------------
Goal: consistent, safe, and performant model packaging and serving across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
- Model artifact: include a model-card.json in the model bundle with fields {model_id, version, architecture, vocab, license, quantization_profile, expected_max_seq_len, operator_contact}.
- Versioning: semantic-like versions (vMAJOR.MINOR[+build]) and immutable model bundles.
- Quantization profiles: maintain validated quantization profiles per architecture under /quantization-profiles; include perf/quality benchmarks for each profile.
- Packaging: OCI-compatible artifact, with image metadata referencing the model_card and dependency constraints.
- Serving interface: all serving endpoints must implement the standardized inference contract: predict(input, max_tokens, stream=false, metadata={}).
- Routing & fallbacks: runtime should support model variant routing by policy (latency, cost, region). Fallbacks must be declared in model_card (fallback_model_id).
- Safety checks: before a model is allowed on Hosted, run automated evals (prompt sets) and a manual quality review for high-risk categories.
- Autoscaling: target P90 CPU/GPU utilization thresholds (see Performance section) and configure cold-start limits for ephemeral nodes.
- Canary & Rollout: models are rolled out via canary traffic (default 1% for 24h) with automated quality monitors; rollback triggers: >5% increase in error rate or quality regression beyond configured drift threshold.

Model bundle example (model-card.json snippet):
{
  "model_id": "redwood-ogl-7b",
  "version": "v1.2.0",
  "architecture": "transformer-decoder",
  "quantization_profile": "q4_0_fast_inference",
  "expected_max_seq_len": "2048",
  "operator_contact": "@ml-onboard"
}

5) Observability Standards
------------------------
All services must be observable by default. Use OpenTelemetry for traces and metrics, and structured JSON logs.
- Traces: instrument request boundaries and cross-service spans for all inference requests. Include trace_id and request_id in logs.
- Metrics: Prometheus-style metrics with the standard prefix for Redwood: rwd_*. Key metric families: rwd_request_total, rwd_request_errors, rwd_latency_seconds_bucket, rwd_tokens_generated_total, rwd_gpu_utilization_percent.
- Tagging/labels: every metric include labels {service, env, model_id, route, deploy_hash}.
- Logs: JSON structured logs with keys {ts, level, service, request_id, trace_id, msg, err_code}. Avoid PII in logs.
- Dashboards: each service must publish a baseline dashboard with availability, latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate, token throughput, and cost per 1k tokens.
- Alerting: alerts should map to runbooks. Base thresholds: error rate > 1% for 5m or p95 latency > 2x baseline for 5m => page SRE. Use severity labels (sev1/sev2/sev3).
- Retention: metrics retained 90 days hot, 365 days cold; logs retained 30 days searchable, 365 days archived.

6) Performance Standards & SLOs
-----------------------------
SLOs are targeted objectives; SLA specifics are contract-dependent (Dedicated/Enterprise).
Company-wide default SLOs (Hosted API):
- Availability: 99.5% monthly uptime for public inference endpoints.
- Latency (first token): p95 <= 350ms for short completion (<=64 tokens), p99 <= 800ms.
- Throughput: per-tenant soft throughput targets enforced by quotas; platform-level throughput should sustain 95th percentile traffic with <20% request queuing.
- Error budget policy: 30-day rolling error budget based on availability SLO; >50% budget burn in 7 days => mitigation plan and freeze on non-critical rollouts.
Dedicated contract baseline (example):
- Availability: 99.9% monthly uptime.
- Latency (first token): p95 <= 200ms (depending on model class and dedicated hardware).
Observability metrics to compute SLOs: availability (rwd_request_success_ratio), latency histograms (rwd_latency_seconds_bucket), error budgets and burn rates.

Baseline thresholds for autoscaling and kernel selection:
| Metric | Trigger | Action |
|--------|---------|--------|
| GPU util % (per node) | > 80% p95 for 5m | Add node / scale-out |
| GPU mem pressure | > 90% | Reject new large-seq requests or route to smaller model variant |
| Queue latency | median queue > 50ms | Increase batch size for throughput-optimized queues |

7) ADRs: Format & Recent Decisions
---------------------------------
ADRs document architecture choices and alternatives. Template (short):
- ADR id: ADR-YYYY-NN
- Title
- Status: proposed | accepted | deprecated | superseded
- Context: problem statement
- Decision: chosen option
- Consequences: operational and technical impacts
- Alternatives considered
- Owners & Reviewers

Recent ADRs (summaries):
- ADR-2025-07: Standardize internal gRPC for high-throughput control-plane services — accepted. Result: lower CPU serialization overhead and stronger proto contracts; cost: more complex build chain.
- ADR-2025-11: Model routing policy defaults to latency-first with cost-aware weights — accepted. Consequence: runtime implements weighted routing and per-tenant overrides.
- ADR-2026-01: OpenTelemetry as canonical tracing library — accepted. All new services must emit OTLP by 2026-06-01.

Sample ADR (full):
- ADR id: ADR-2026-02
- Title: Default to OpenAPI v3 for public REST surfaces
- Status: accepted
- Context: inconsistent REST schemas across services caused client regressions and tooling drift.
- Decision: all public REST endpoints must publish OpenAPI v3 specs in the repo and expose a /openapi.json endpoint. CI enforces schema generation and a consumer compatibility test.
- Consequences: Single source of truth for SDK generation; small initial engineering effort to add schema gen to two legacy services.
- Alternatives: continue ad-hoc JSON schema per service (rejected), use GraphQL (rejected for operational complexity).
- Owners: API Platform team; Reviewers: SDK, Security, and Product.

8) Change & Rollout Process
--------------------------
- Non-breaking changes: standard PR -> CI -> canary (0->100% over 24h) with monitoring.
- Breaking changes: create ADR, announce in architecture channel, schedule migration window, provide backward compat shim for at least 30 days.
- Emergency rollback: SREs may perform immediate rollback and must file a post-action review within 48h.

9) Ownership & Contacts
----------------------
- Architecture WG (owners of this doc): eng-architecture@internal.redwood.com (aliases).
- API Platform: @api-platform; Model Onboarding: @ml-onboard; Infra: @eng-infra; SRE: @eng-sre.
- For ADRs and exceptions: open a PR under /eng-architecture/adr and tag reviewers.

Appendix A: Runbook links & references
------------------------------------
- Runtime architecture: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture
- Terraform modules: /confluence/eng-infra/terraform-modules
- SLOs & Error Budgets: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets
- Model onboarding checklist: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding

Appendix B: Quick checklist for new changes
-----------------------------------------
1. Create/verify OpenAPI spec (public APIs).
2. Add/validate unit + integration tests.
3. Add metrics + traces (OTel), ensure logs are structured.
4. Add IaC changes as modular Terraform; run tfplan and security scans.
5. Update model_card for model-related changes.
6. Draft ADR if cross-cutting or breaking.
7. Register rollout plan, canary criteria, and rollback steps in PR template.

This document will be reviewed quarterly by the Architecture WG or earlier if major platform changes occur.
